intended_object: The canonical ring isomorphism A / ker(A → ∏ᵢ kᵢ) ≅ ∏ᵢ kᵢ. Here A = ⋂ᵢ O_{vᵢ} is the intersection of the valuation rings of finitely many pairwise inequivalent rank-one valuations vᵢ on a field K, and kᵢ are their residue fields. This is the Chinese-remainder / approximation-theorem description of A modulo its Jacobson radical. I inferred this from the docstring, the name and the surrounding file.
explanation:
The body applies `RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective` to `intersectionResidueProduct val`. That map is `RingHom.pi` of the residue maps on `intersectionSubring val = ⨅ i, (val i).valuationSubring`. Its surjectivity, `intersectionResidueProduct_surjective`, is proved in the library from an approximation theorem, using finiteness of ι, rank one and pairwise inequivalence. So the result is exactly the first-isomorphism-theorem identification of the quotient by the joint residue kernel with the full product of residue fields, as the docstring says.

The hypotheses are needed: without them the residue map need not be surjective. For example, two equivalent valuations give the diagonal, not the whole product. The same statement holds for pairwise incomparable valuation rings of arbitrary rank (Bourbaki's semilocal intersection theorem), and for rank-one valuations incomparability is the same as inequivalence. However, the rank-one, pairwise-inequivalent setting is the standard one for the approximation theorem, and it is the setting the whole module works in. The construction is canonical and correct there.

Mathlib has no dedicated counterpart. Only the generic `RingHom.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective` exists, and this definition is an instance of it.
